questions.question: Which of the following distracts drivers and increases crash risk?

options.text: CD player
Radio
Cell phone
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Cell phones, radios, and CD players are all dangerous distractions that increase crash risk.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on major highways?

options.text: Stay alert.
Keep your eyes moving.
Be ready to react to road hazards.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: On highways, stay alert and keep your eyes moving. Don't stare at one thing for more than a few seconds. Be ready to react to unexpected hazards.

questions.question: You feel angry after something at work. What should you do before driving home?

options.text: Play the radio loudly so you won't think about it.
Drive fast on the highway to let off steam.
Take a few minutes to calm down before you start driving.
Stop at a bar and have a few drinks before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down before you start driving.
questions.explanation: If you are upset or angry, take time to calm down before driving. Driving while angry is dangerous to you and others on the road.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights is nearby. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to avoid the emergency vehicle.
Stop immediately and block their path.
Move to the side of the road to give them a clear path.
Signal when it's clear for them to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the side of the road to give them a clear path.
questions.explanation: Always make space for emergency vehicles. Pull to the side of the road if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Where are U-turns not allowed?

options.text: In a curve in the road.
On a hill where you can't see 500 feet ahead in both directions.
Near a sign that says no U-turns.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: U-turns are not allowed in curves, on hills with poor visibility (less than 500 feet in each direction), or near signs that prohibit U-turns.

questions.question: You drink alcohol socially. What is the safest way to get home?

options.text: Drink coffee before driving.
Get a ride from a friend who hasn't been drinking.
Take a cold shower before driving.
Wait 30 minutes before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a ride from a friend who hasn't been drinking.
questions.explanation: The safest choice is to ride home with a sober friend. Coffee and cold showers don't reduce alcohol in your blood. Your body needs about one hour to eliminate alcohol from one drink.

questions.question: What is important when changing lanes?

options.text: Signal before you change lanes.
Check your blind spot.
Make sure the lane is clear.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder. Make sure the lane is clear before you move.

questions.question: Is checking your blind spot before changing lanes a good habit?

options.text: No, it's a bad habit.
Yes, it's a good habit.
No, it's not necessary.
No, not if you use your mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it's a good habit.
questions.explanation: Checking your blind spot by looking over your shoulder is a good habit. Don't rely only on mirrors.

questions.question: When should you check that your passengers have buckled their seat belts?

options.text: Only in bad weather.
Before you start the engine.
When a police officer stops you.
Only on long trips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start the engine.
questions.explanation: Seat belts save lives in a crash. Make sure you and all passengers are buckled up before you start driving.

questions.question: How much longer does it take to stop on slippery roads?

options.text: About the same as on dry roads.
A little shorter than on dry roads.
Two to 10 times longer than on dry roads.
No difference.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two to 10 times longer than on dry roads.
questions.explanation: Stopping on slippery roads takes two to 10 times longer than on dry pavement. Drive slowly and carefully on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Roundabout ahead.
Lane ends, merge left.
Turn around.
Curve ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Roundabout ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a roundabout is coming. Enter slowly and yield to cars already in the roundabout.

questions.question: When in a travel lane on the roadway:

options.text: You may stop to drop off passengers.
You may stop to look up an address.
You may make a U-turn or back up if you get on the wrong entrance ramp of the freeway.
Don't stop for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't stop for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.
questions.explanation: Never stop in a travel lane. Keep driving until you can safely leave the road. If you miss your turn or exit, do not back up. Go to the next turn or exit.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing with no warning signals, a driver should slow down, look, and listen.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: At railroad crossings with no warning devices, slow down and look both ways. Listen for trains. Only cross when it is safe.

questions.question: Motorcycles are entitled to:

options.text: The bicycle lane.
The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.
The width of the sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to use the full width of a lane, just like other vehicles.

questions.question: Night driving is more difficult than day driving because:

options.text: Cars overheat more quickly at night.
Visibility is reduced in the dark.
It is more likely to be raining at night.
You are more likely to encounter a motorcycle at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Visibility is reduced in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far ahead. Use your headlights and drive slowly enough to stop within the distance you can see.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No turns are allowed on this road.
The road narrows ahead.
There are a series of curves ahead.
The road may be slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: There are a series of curves ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a winding road with three or more curves ahead.

questions.question: Highway hypnosis can result from:

options.text: Staring at the roadway for long periods of time.
Frequent rest stops.
Too much sleep the night before your trip.
Short trips on expressways.

questions.correctAnswerText: Staring at the roadway for long periods of time.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis occurs when you stare straight ahead for too long and stop looking around you. This makes you zone out and likely to crash into traffic ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road to the right is for one-way traffic only.
Due to roadwork, there is a detour to the right.
Slow down because the road ahead curves sharply.
There is a crossroad to your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down because the road ahead curves sharply.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the road ahead has a sharp curve. Slow down before reaching the curve.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing and you do not see or hear a train. You must stop:

options.text: If a stop sign is posted.
If a crossing gate is lowered.
If the crossing lights are flashing.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing if flashing red lights are on, a gate is down, a stop sign is posted, or a flagger signals you to stop. Never race a train.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You are about to enter a one-way street the wrong way.
School crossing ahead.
Do not drive in this lane.
Traffic turning left on the green light must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic turning left on the green light must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that left-turning traffic must wait for oncoming traffic to pass, even when the light is green.

questions.question: When sharing the road with large commercial vehicles, you should:

options.text: Know that large vehicles need extra time and space to slow down and stop.
Know that commercial vehicles have large blind spots.
Signal your turns and lane changes well in advance.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Large trucks and buses have air brakes that work slower than regular brakes. They need more time and space to stop. Large vehicles have bigger blind spots than cars. Always signal before turning or changing lanes.

questions.question: A steady green light means you:

options.text: Must slow down and get ready to stop.
Must stop and check for traffic before going.
Can drive through if the road is clear.
Cannot turn right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can drive through if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you can go through the intersection if no traffic or pedestrians are in your way. You can turn right or left on a green light unless a sign says you cannot. Always let other vehicles and pedestrians go first when turning.

questions.question: A seat belt should be adjusted so that it:

options.text: Is loose.
Fits snug across your hip bones and lower belly.
Is hidden under the seat.
Stops the seat belt alarm from going off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fits snug across your hip bones and lower belly.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower belly. The shoulder belt should sit comfortably so you can fit your fist between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: Not getting enough sleep affects your driving the same way as:

options.text: Drinking alcohol.
Taking amphetamines.
Feeling angry.
Driving with teenagers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drinking alcohol.
questions.explanation: Lack of sleep harms your driving ability just like alcohol does. Being awake for 18 hours affects driving like a 0.05% blood alcohol level. Being awake for 24 hours affects driving like a 0.10% blood alcohol level.

questions.question: Don't follow cars too closely because:

options.text: You cannot see the road between the cars.
You may not have time to stop if the car in front stops suddenly.
You cannot see the turn signals.
You cannot see the brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not have time to stop if the car in front stops suddenly.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely and the car ahead stops suddenly, you may crash into it because you won't have time to stop.

questions.question: A sign of a drunk driver is:

options.text: Weaving between lanes.
Driving slower than the traffic around them.
Making sudden stops.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include speeding, weaving, driving slower than other cars, jerking movements, and sudden stops.

questions.question: When getting ready to turn left, you should:

options.text: Slow down gradually while checking your rearview mirror.
Move into the left lane.
Watch for oncoming cars and pedestrians.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before turning left, signal 3 to 5 seconds ahead. Check your rearview mirror and slow down gradually. On a multi-lane road, move into the left lane before the intersection. Wait for traffic and pedestrians to clear, then turn when it is safe.

questions.question: When you see a school bus stopped with its stop arm out, you should:

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait.
Honk your horn and pass on the left.
Keep driving when you think the kids are done getting off.
Pass the bus before the door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when you see a stopped school bus with its stop arm out. Do not go until the stop arm is put away.

questions.question: Drivers do not have to let pedestrians cross in a marked crosswalk.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You must stop and let pedestrians cross in a marked crosswalk. You must also stop for pedestrians crossing in an unmarked crosswalk on your side of the road when there are no traffic lights.

questions.question: When a curb is painted ____, it marks a handicap parking space.

options.text: Yellow
Blue
White
Green

questions.correctAnswerText: Blue
questions.explanation: Painted curbs show parking rules. A blue curb marks a handicap parking space. Only people with a handicap license plate or tag can park there.
